shadow:
Notice how quickly the hand reaches. A phone, a fridge door, a tab, a small new thing to look at. The reach happens before the wanting is even felt. That is distraction, and it is not a weakness of character. It is the senses doing what they were built to do, pulling attention outward toward the next bit of colour and sound.

There is an ache underneath all that reaching. Most people never get a clear look at it, because the moment it surfaces, something else is already happening on the screen. The world is generous with that something else. It hands you gossip, scrolling, plans, a hundred small errands of the eye, each one promising the dull feeling will lift if you just look a little longer.

It does not lift. The reach feeds the ache, the ache makes you reach again. People treat the restlessness as the problem and manage it with more input. That is the loop turning. But the loop has a seam. It shows the moment the screen goes dark and the room is just a room. The ache is right there, plain, and that bare moment is the way out, waiting to be felt instead of fled.
repressive: Some go grey and stop reaching at all. The spark for anything dims down, days blur into a flat sameness, and this dullness gets mistaken for who they simply are. It is not who they are. It is a fire banked too low.
reactive: Others keep the input loud. New trip, new screen, new relationship, anything moving fast enough that the quiet underneath never gets a hearing. They look busy, even alive. Nothing has actually been let in.
gift:
Something shifts when a person stops running from the bare moment. The ache does not vanish. It just stops being an emergency, and once it is no longer an emergency, a different skill becomes possible. Choosing what to let in.

This is enrichment. It is not abstaining. It is the difference between what feeds you and what only fills you, felt clearly enough to act on. The cake you would genuinely enjoy is sometimes worth eating and sometimes not, and you can tell which without a rule deciding for you. The senses stay open. They are just no longer in charge.

There is a test for whether the loop still has you. Is there anything you cannot say no to. Whatever it is, that thing still owns a piece of you. Enrichment is getting that piece back, by learning where your energy actually leaks out and sealing it.

The surprising part is what happens with the energy you stop spending outward. It turns. It goes looking inward instead of out, and finds a quieter fire there. You start finding flavour in things other people walk past as ordinary. Boredom stops being something to escape, and out of that quiet comes the thing worth saying.
siddhi:
Here the loop has fully reversed. The same pull that once chased every passing flicker now drinks from one source only, and that source is the heart itself. The arrow that pierces is love, and a person at this frequency keeps getting pierced and keeps welcoming it.

This is intoxication. Not the dulling kind. The kind that makes someone luminous and slightly impossible, drunk on a wine that pours from inside them and never runs out. They take life in fully, a sip of the world enough to set off the deeper joy, suffering folded in alongside pleasure because both can be tasted.

They have noticed there is no point to any of it, and instead of despair this lands as delight. The searching is over. What is left is wonder, laughter, a love that spreads to whoever sits near it.

Look back from here at the restless reaching of the start. All that hunger was love with the wrong address. It was always trying to find this. It just kept knocking on the world when the door was here.
